Yes. Current release history is at root [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), while Sepo release/versioning automation is already centered on `.agent`, especially [`.agent/package.json`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/package.json), [`.agent/docs/technical-details/versioning.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/versioning.md), [`.agent/src/cli/prepare-release.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/prepare-release.ts), and [`.github/prompts/agent-release.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-release.md).

Recommended implementation:

1. Move `CHANGELOG.md` to `.agent/CHANGELOG.md`, preserving the existing `0.1.0` entry.
2. Update `.github/prompts/agent-release.md` so future release PRs explicitly update `.agent/CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Update `.agent/src/cli/prepare-release.ts` acceptance criteria so generated release issues name `.agent/CHANGELOG.md`.
4. Update `.agent/docs/technical-details/versioning.md` to document `.agent/CHANGELOG.md` as the canonical Sepo changelog.
5. Adjust any focused release-prep tests that assert generated issue text.

I’d avoid keeping a duplicate root changelog unless the project wants a short pointer file; moving it fully into `.agent` best matches the request.
